$comment: Regression matrix for the individual/ module set. Each entry pins one proposition that a review caught as WRONG or MISSING, so that a future editorial pass cannot silently delete it. `anchors` are literal substrings that must all be present in `owner`. `forbidden` are regexes for the known-wrong formulation; if one matches, the correction has been reverted. `warn_required` asserts the point-of-use marker (authority.md) sits in the same structural block (list item / table row / paragraph, fences excluded) as `marker_anchor` — which is mandatory once a warn-required entry has more than one anchor. `scope` is mandatory for multi-anchor entries: "local" enforces that all anchors sit in one block, "distributed" records a deliberate spread. `no_restatement_outside_owner` regexes are scanned across the OTHER individual modules to enforce a sole-ownership claim. Run: python3 -B evals/validate_individual_matrix.py

entries.proposition: §121 nonqualified use is prorated over TOTAL ownership, and §121(b)(5)(C)(ii)(I) excepts only TRAILING non-use within the five-year window — rental before the last residency period still counts.
anchors:
do not
   apply a categorical rule in either direction
entries.failure_mode: Either overstates gain (counting trailing rental) or understates it (exempting pre-residency rental).

entries.proposition: §121(b)(2) is asymmetric on MFJ: either spouse may meet ownership, both must meet use; failing use as to one spouse falls to the sum of separately computed amounts, not zero.
entries.origin: post-cut regression audit; found MISSING again by the regression matrix build
entries.failure_mode: Denies the exclusion entirely when one spouse fails the use test, instead of allowing the single-filer amount.

entries.proposition: A prior §1031 exchange bars §121 for five years — a threshold disqualifier tested before any computation.
entries.failure_mode: Computes an exclusion that is unavailable.

entries.proposition: §121(d)(6) basis reduction is depreciation ALLOWED BUT NOT LESS THAN ALLOWABLE; unclaimed depreciation for 2+ years is corrected by Form 3115 with a §481(a) adjustment, not an amended return.
anchors: allowed, but not less than allowable
entries.failure_mode: Understates recapture, or sends the taxpayer down a barred amendment path.

entries.proposition: On a converted residence, basis for LOSS is the lesser of FMV at conversion or adjusted basis.
entries.failure_mode: Claims a loss that personal-use appreciation history does not support.

entries.proposition: Inherited ROTH IRAs take no annual RMDs in years 1-9; the owner is always treated as dying before the RBD.
entries.failure_mode: Forces distributions that destroy ten years of tax-free growth.

entries.proposition: SEPP from a QUALIFIED PLAN requires separation from service; an in-service SEPP from a current employer's 401(k) is penalized.
entries.failure_mode: Recommends a penalized distribution stream.

entries.proposition: A qualified Roth distribution requires the five-year clock AND a §408A(d)(2)(A) triggering event. Five years alone is not enough.
entries.failure_mode: Treats a taxable distribution as tax-free.

entries.proposition: §465(e) recapture has TWO legs — income under (e)(1)(A) and a deduction in the succeeding year under (e)(1)(B).
entries.failure_mode: Permanently overstates tax by booking the income and never the offsetting deduction.

entries.proposition: PREDICATE: qualified nonrecourse financing exists only for an activity of HOLDING REAL PROPERTY. Nonrecourse debt in equipment, oil-and-gas, or operating funds is never QNRF.
entries.failure_mode: Grants at-risk basis for non-real-property nonrecourse debt — an unbounded number, because the mechanics that follow it survived the cut.

entries.proposition: A RELATED person can be a qualified person for QNRF where the financing is commercially reasonable and on substantially the same terms as unrelated lending.
entries.failure_mode: A flat unrelated-lender test denies at-risk basis the statute grants.

entries.proposition: A related-party sale DEFERS suspended passive losses; it does not extinguish them.
entries.failure_mode: Writes off a live carryforward as dead.

entries.proposition: ORDERING: released §469 losses go first against that activity, then against other passive income, then against nonpassive.
anchors: then** against net income from **all other passive
entries.failure_mode: Releasing straight against wages skips step 2 and understates how much other suspended loss is freed.

entries.proposition: The §469(i) modified-AGI definition is owned here: AGI without IRA deductions, taxable SS, §221, §199A, §911, and the passive losses themselves.
entries.origin: post-cut regression audit (the MAGI register in 1040.md §4 pointed at a definition that had been cut)
entries.failure_mode: The MAGI register dangles; ordinary AGI gets substituted and the $25,000 allowance phases out at the wrong point.

entries.proposition: §469 material-participation / STR status does NOT determine SE tax under §1402. The two are independent.
anchors: §469 status does not determine SE tax
entries.failure_mode: Wrong Schedule SE in both directions on short-term rentals.

entries.proposition: §213(d)(5) treats a child of divorced or separated parents as a dependent of EACH parent — BOTH deduct what they actually paid, regardless of Form 8332.
entries.origin: family-CPA review — an earlier Codex-driven 'fix' had made this worse
entries.marker_anchor: §213(d)(5) treats a child of divorced or separated parents as a
anchors: §213(d)(5) treats a child of divorced or separated parents as a

entries.proposition: §25A FOLLOWS THE DEPENDENCY CLAIM under §25A(g)(3); it is not itself an item released by Form 8332. It moves as a consequence of the release, not as a released item.
entries.origin: cpa-review vs codex-signoff-5 conflict — resolved by stating the mechanism
anchors: §25A keys to whoever claims the student
entries.failure_mode: Either answer stated flatly is wrong for the most common divorced-parent pattern.

entries.proposition: §6015(f) equitable relief HAS a deadline — before the §6502 collection statute expires, or within the §6511 refund period.
entries.failure_mode: 'No deadline' costs a taxpayer relief they were entitled to.

entries.proposition: §471(c) is NOT an expensing election — it does not license deducting unsold inventory. Adopting it initially is not a method CHANGE requiring Form 3115.
entries.origin: cpa-review-1; refined by codex-signoff-6 (the Form 3115 overstatement)
anchors: §471(c) is not a license to deduct unsold inventory
entries.failure_mode: Invites deducting unsold inventory, or blocks a permissible initial method.

entries.proposition: ISO status post-termination is §422(a)(2)'s three months. The plan's post-termination exercise period is a separate contractual term; a 10-year PTEP does not extend §422.
entries.failure_mode: Treats an NSO exercise as an ISO — wrong AMT and wrong ordinary income.

entries.proposition: The age-55 exception turns on the SEPARATION date, not the distribution date; rolling to an IRA destroys it and NUA permanently.
anchors: separation date, not the distribution date
entries.failure_mode: Destroys the only penalty-free pre-59½ access the taxpayer has.

entries.proposition: Digital-asset ABANDONMENT losses are barred by §67(h) (a miscellaneous itemized deduction); THEFT losses survive via §67(b)(3). Both arise under §165(c)(2) — the distinction is the §67 gate, not the loss provision.
anchors: theft survives and abandonment does not
entries.failure_mode: Claims a disallowed abandonment loss, or forfeits an allowable theft loss.

entries.proposition: Notice 2025-7 and Notice 2026-20 provide lot-identification relief; 2026-20 extends it through 12/31/2026.
entries.origin: digital-asset specialist review — guidance the author did not know existed
entries.failure_mode: Forces FIFO where books-and-records identification is permitted.

entries.proposition: §1091 reaches 'stock or securities'; digital assets are property, so wash sales do not apply — BUT crypto ETPs and crypto-related equities ARE securities and §1091 applies in full.
entries.failure_mode: Harvesting an ETP loss and rebuying is a wash sale; a blanket 'crypto is exempt' rule gets it wrong.

entries.proposition: PTP amount realized includes §752(d) liability relief; the §751 ordinary component is computed INDEPENDENTLY and is not a carve-out of total gain, so the remainder is frequently a capital LOSS.
anchors: not a carve-out of total gain
entries.failure_mode: Understates gain, then mischaracterizes the remainder as capital gain when it is a loss.

entries.proposition: Worker classification is a legal DETERMINATION, not a tax election. Form 8919 vs Schedule C is not a taxpayer choice.
anchors: Classification is a determination, not an election
forbidden: choose between Form 8919 and Schedule C
entries.failure_mode: Frames a legal test as a planning lever.

entries.proposition: TWO bonus-depreciation regimes coexist in 2025 — acquisition date selects the regime, placed-in-service year selects the legacy percentage. Acquisition date alone cannot select the percentage.
entries.failure_mode: Applies 100% bonus to property acquired before 1/19/2025, or the phase-down to property acquired after.

entries.proposition: CAP: §179 cannot exceed aggregate taxable income from the active conduct of a trade or business, cannot create a loss, and the disallowed amount carries forward indefinitely. Bonus has no such limit and CAN create a loss — this is what decides the election.
entries.origin: post-cut regression audit; found STILL MISSING by the regression matrix build
entries.failure_mode: Produces an unbounded §179 deduction, and generates a carryforward that three other files (1040.md §5, year-over-year.md, carryforwards.json) already expect but nothing computes.

entries.proposition: CAP: §108(a)(3) limits the insolvency exclusion to the amount of insolvency immediately BEFORE the discharge. A taxpayer insolvent by $1 excludes $1.
entries.origin: post-cut regression audit (the worksheet survived, the cap did not)
entries.failure_mode: Excludes the entire discharge on a showing of any insolvency — an unbounded exclusion.

entries.proposition: QPRI (§108(a)(1)(E)/§108(h)) is NOT permanent and was not extended by OBBBA; insolvency IS permanent. Never present them as a matched pair.
anchors: it as a matched pair with insolvency
entries.failure_mode: Claims an expired exclusion for the target year.

entries.proposition: A 1099-A is a DISPOSITION, not COD. Nonrecourse: amount realized is the full debt (Tufts). Recourse: BIFURCATE into disposition (FMV vs basis) plus COD (debt minus FMV).
entries.origin: architecture audit — COD had no owning module
entries.marker_anchor: A 1099-A is a disposition, not COD
anchors: A 1099-A is a disposition, not COD
entries.failure_mode: Reports COD only, missing a Schedule D / 4797 event entirely.

entries.proposition: Capital loss carryover is reduced by the amount ALLOWABLE, not the amount that produced a benefit — a zero-tax year still consumes it.
entries.failure_mode: Overstates the carryforward into every subsequent year.

entries.proposition: A math-error notice carries a hard 60-day window to request abatement under §6213(b)(2); missing it forfeits the deficiency procedures.
entries.failure_mode: Loses Tax Court access on an assessment that could have been abated.

entries.proposition: §6501(c)(8) suspends the period on the ENTIRE return, but reasonable cause can limit the suspension to related items.
entries.origin: codex-signoff-6 (compression distortion — the qualifier had been cut)
anchors: reasonable cause can limit it to related items
entries.failure_mode: Overstates the exposure and the hold.

entries.proposition: Form 8283 Section B may be transmitted on e-file as a PDF attachment OR by mail with Form 8453 — it is not Form 8453-exclusive.
entries.failure_mode: Sends the taxpayer down an unnecessary paper path.

entries.proposition: The §170(f)(11) readily-valued-property exception does NOT reach digital assets — they are not securities. CCA 202302012 also rejected reasonable cause.

entries.proposition: SUBSTANTIATION IS NOT CURABLE: a §170(f)(8) CWA must be obtained by the EARLIER of filing or the due date. One obtained during examination is too late.
entries.origin: module build; flagged by cpa-review-1 as the highest-frequency real loss
entries.failure_mode: The deduction is lost and no remediation exists.

entries.proposition: The §111 tax-benefit rule must be COMPUTED, not assumed — with the SALT cap binding or the standard deduction taken, a state refund is frequently not taxable at all.
entries.failure_mode: Taxes a refund that produced no benefit.

entries.proposition: The §163(d)(4)(B)(iii) election trades the preferential rate on qualified dividends/LTCG for a current ordinary deduction. Record it as a decision with the arithmetic both ways. The §163(d) NII figure is NOT the §1411 NIIT base.
entries.failure_mode: Silently surrenders preferential rates, or reuses the wrong base for NIIT.

entries.proposition: §1014(b)(6): community property receives a FULL step-up on BOTH halves. This file owns the rule.
entries.origin: module build; ownership assigned by architecture audit
entries.failure_mode: Halves the step-up for a community-property couple, or duplicates the rule in state-residency.md.

entries.proposition: Rev. Rul. 2023-2: assets in a completed-gift irrevocable grantor trust not includible in the gross estate get NO §1014 adjustment.
entries.failure_mode: Assumes a step-up the ruling denies — the whole planning conclusion inverts.

entries.proposition: §1014(e) denies the step-up where appreciated property was gifted to a decedent within one year and returns to the donor OR THE DONOR'S SPOUSE. The spouse variant is the one the strategy actually uses.
entries.failure_mode: Blesses the exact transaction the anti-abuse rule targets.

entries.proposition: Portability requires a timely Form 706, but Rev. Proc. 2022-32 allows a LATE election within five years of death for estates not otherwise required to file.
entries.failure_mode: Writes off a recoverable multi-million-dollar exclusion as permanently lost.

entries.proposition: DSUE is available only from the LAST deceased spouse; remarriage plus a second spousal death wipes out a banked DSUE. GST exemption is not portable.
entries.failure_mode: Relies on an exclusion that no longer exists.

entries.proposition: §2503(e) covers TUITION ONLY — not books, supplies, room or board — and must be paid DIRECTLY to the institution.
entries.failure_mode: Treats room and board as an excluded transfer, consuming exclusion the donor thought was free.

entries.proposition: Before recommending a phased-out parent forgo the dependency so the student claims AOTC: §25A(b)(4)(B) bars a student subject to the kiddie tax from the 40% refundable portion — usually the entire point of the move.
entries.failure_mode: Recommends a strategy whose entire benefit is statutorily barred.

entries.proposition: The 1099-Q goes to the RECIPIENT of the distribution. Paid to the beneficiary or the school it carries the beneficiary's TIN, and taxable earnings land on the STUDENT's return.
entries.failure_mode: Puts 529 earnings on the wrong return — one of the most common real 529 errors.

entries.proposition: §135 savings bonds: the bond must be issued in the name of the taxpayer (or taxpayer and spouse) who was 24+ at issuance. A bond in the CHILD's name never qualifies at any age.
entries.failure_mode: Claims an exclusion the ownership rule kills outright.

entries.proposition: §221 requires LEGAL OBLIGATION — a parent paying a loan in the child's name gets nothing. The planning answer: treat the payment as a gift to the student, who is then treated as paying the interest and may deduct it if not claimed as a dependent.
entries.failure_mode: Loses the deduction entirely when a compliant path existed.

entries.proposition: OWNERSHIP: kiddie-dependents.md §2 is the SOLE owner of how a taxable scholarship is characterized for §1(g) and Form 8615. education.md must not restate it — the §1(g) threshold test and the Form 8615 computation treat it differently.
entries.origin: architecture audit — the two files contradicted each other
entries.failure_mode: Two files give different answers to the fact that decides the whole scholarship-allocation strategy.

entries.failure_mode: Treats a fully taxable transfer as nonrecognition.

entries.proposition: The §72(t)(2)(C) QDRO penalty exception applies to a distribution FROM THE PLAN to the alternate payee. Rolling it into an IRA destroys the exception permanently.
anchors: Rolling it into an IRA destroys the exception permanently
entries.failure_mode: Destroys often the only penalty-free pre-59½ access that spouse has.

entries.proposition: Carryforwards die with the decedent. §469(g)(2) allows suspended passive losses on the final return only to the extent they EXCEED the step-up.
entries.failure_mode: Passes carryforwards to an estate or survivor that cannot use them, or overstates the final-return deduction.

entries.proposition: §66(c) is a DISTINCT regime from §6015 for community-property spouses, and is often the applicable path. Form 8379 injured spouse is neither.
entries.failure_mode: Files the wrong relief request, often after the other regime's window has closed.

entries.proposition: Charitable carryover is YEAR-CROSSING state tracked BY CLASS in carryforwards.json, not in an annual workpaper. A single aggregate carryover is insufficient.
entries.failure_mode: Five-year classes collapse into one number and expire in the wrong order.

entries.proposition: ORDERING: §108(a)(2)(C) applies QPRI BEFORE insolvency unless the taxpayer elects otherwise. Listing QPRI last inverts the statutory default.
entries.origin: independent audit of the second-cut proposal, 2026-08-29
anchors: Listing QPRI last inverts the default
entries.failure_mode: Applies insolvency first, consuming the insolvency amount and wasting a QPRI exclusion that applies by default — and reverses the attribute-reduction consequences.

entries.proposition: CAPS: §108(c)(2)(A) limits the QRPBI exclusion to principal over FMV of the securing property; §108(c)(2)(B) further caps it at aggregate adjusted bases of depreciable real property.
entries.origin: independent audit — identical shape to the §108(a)(3) regression
entries.failure_mode: The QRPBI election is retained as a mechanic with no ceiling — an unbounded exclusion.

entries.proposition: FLOOR: §1017(b)(2) caps the §108(b) basis reduction at the excess of aggregate bases over aggregate liabilities immediately after the discharge.
entries.failure_mode: Over-reduces basis, converting an exclusion into a larger future gain than the statute requires.

entries.proposition: FLOORS: a personal casualty loss surviving the §165(h)(5) declared-disaster gate is still reduced by $100 PER EVENT (§165(h)(1)) and then allowed only above 10% of AGI (§165(h)(2)).
entries.origin: independent audit — the gate survived the cut, both floors did not
entries.failure_mode: A qualifying disaster loss is deducted in full — an unbounded number, while the workpaper schema and life-events.md both already reference the deduction.

entries.proposition: The charitable CLASS TAXONOMY and ORDER OF APPLICATION are mechanics this file owns; only the percentages belong to authority.md. A crowded-out gift carries forward in its own class on its own clock.
entries.origin: independent audit — the file asserted 'the limits stack in order' and supplied no order, contradicting its own charter

entries.proposition: The §529 10%-penalty waivers split in two: DEATH AND DISABILITY ARE UNCAPPED; tax-free assistance, service-academy, and §25A-coordination are AMOUNT-LIMITED. The assistance waiver is §530(d)(4)(B)(iii) — NOT (ii), which is disability — and incorporates the WHOLE §25A(g)(2) list, materially broader than scholarships. The list itself is NOT paraphrased here: it must be read from primary authority at point of use. Excludability from gross income is the operative condition. Earnings remain taxable in every case.
entries.origin: codex-signoff-8 P0 ('each waiver is capped'), signoff-9 P0 (broader than scholarship), signoff-10 P0 (chapter 1606, enrollment branch, (ii)/(iii) miscite), signoff-11 P0 (§117 excludability), signoff-12 P0 (§117(c)(2) carve-outs). FOUR consecutive wrong paraphrases of one statutory list is itself the finding: on Codex's direct recommendation the enumeration was REPLACED by a point-of-use pointer, which cannot drift.
anchors:
Read §25A(g)(2) from primary authority at
  point of use
forbidden: service scholarship\s+paid for teaching or research
entries.failure_mode: Understates the penalty waiver by reading the assistance category as scholarships only; cites the disability subparagraph for the assistance rule; or re-introduces an inline paraphrase of §25A(g)(2), which has been wrong on every attempt.

entries.proposition: QPRI reaches a discharge before the statutory cutoff OR ONE SUBJECT TO AN ARRANGEMENT ENTERED INTO AND EVIDENCED IN WRITING BEFORE THAT DATE. A workout agreed in writing before the cutoff qualifies even though the discharge falls after it.

Investment real property does not qualify.
